search_log: Searched “The Woman in the Window A.J. Finn official excerpt first chapter” and opened the WTTW-hosted typeset opening sample.
Searched “The Woman in the Window A.J. Finn first person narrator point of view” and opened explicit whole-book analyses and reviews.
Searched “site:harpercollins.com The Woman in the Window excerpt A.J. Finn”; the publisher result led to the Literary Hub excerpt credited as used with William Morrow’s permission.
Searched Google Books for the title and author; the accessible page supplied publication metadata and synopsis but no additional diagnostic sustained prose, so it was not used as person evidence.
Targeted checks for narrator and alternating point of view found consistent descriptions of Anna as the sole first-person narrator and no credible evidence of sustained sections in another person.
person_note: The quote set repeatedly exposes Anna Fox as a participating “I” narrator in present action, memory, observation, and interior response. Dialogue, film quotations, generic advice, and aphoristic material were treated as local or non-base rather than as competing persons; several bare descriptions of “she” were left unmarked because they are compatible with Anna’s first-person narration. Two sustained authorized or publisher-derived excerpts independently show the same first-person voice in the opening and an interior passage, while multiple whole-book sources explicitly identify Anna as the first-person narrator. No credible source indicates alternating base narration, so the controlling person is FIRST with high confidence.
